title: An HF-ordering over a partial subsystem exists exactly when that subsystem can be made an initial segment
author: Silvia Barbina; Enrique Casanovas
work: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 333-335: for partial Steiner triple systems A contained in B, there is an HF-ordering of B over A exactly when there is an HF-ordering of B in which A is an initial segment, and the author adds that one may in fact assume the given order is preserved. One direction is immediate from the definitions. In the other, the argument is not a definition chase: one has to take an element below an element of A that lies outside A, examine the block it produces in the ordering and extract four distinct elements, each of which is either below the chosen element or inside A, and only then does the defining condition of an HF-ordering over A deliver the contradiction. The statement records the equivalence and neither the block analysis nor the contradiction.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
